newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ford Australia posts record 1996 net, sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ford Australia posts record 1996 net, sales.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Ford Motor Co of Australia Ltd said on Thursday its net after-tax profit rose to a record A$217.3 million (US$167.3 million) in calendar 1996 from the previous record of A$201.7 million in 1995.
Sales also rose to a record A$3.36 billion from the previous peak of A$3.34 billion in 1995, Ford Australia said.

"The profit, in a year in which Ford took overall market leadership for the second year in a row and passenger market leadership for the 15th year, further underpins the company's A$1 billion investment in the next Australian Falcon," it said.
However, its total vehicle sales eased to 132,200 in 1996 from 137,800 in 1995 and its market share to 20.3 percent from 21.5 percent, Ford said.
Ford said the wholly locally designed and produced Falcon family of cars and light commercial vehicles was again the cornerstone of its market leadership and profits.

Ford Australia's president David Morgan said the fact Australian car buyers continued to vote strongly for local product in the face of intense import competition was a major factor in the 1996 result.

"There were external factors as well. Significantly, 1996 was the second strongest year in history for the Australian automotive industry, while the strength of the Australian dollar throughout the year also contributed markedly," he said in a statement.
He said Ford had again set aggressive targets for 1997 to further enhance the business, adding that it was again the market leader in both the overall and passenger vehicle markets in January, 1997.
Ford Australia is a wholly-owned Ford subsidiary.
